extracted.intended_audience: local government officials and municipal communications/public_relations staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for municipal officials and communications staff on writing, formatting, and distributing local government press releases that inform and engage constituents. Covers content elements, tone, accessibility, and distribution channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings For Readability
rubrics_metrics.description: The heading of a press release is important for grabbing the attention of your reader. Constituents should feel engaged from the first line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Header should adequately summarize the main announcement in about 10–15 words and use understandable language for all readers. Aim for an attention‑grabbing but clear headline that conveys the core news.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Relevant Information About The Subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The substance of a press release is key. A press release should be clear and concise, and only contain the most necessary information about a subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elaborate on the announcement, provide details or quotes from relevant parties (e.g., local government leaders), and include any additional information important to constituents. Include essential facts (who, what, when, where, why) and avoid extraneous material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Tone and Grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining a professional tone in a press release is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional tone and correct grammar build credibility, respect, and trust. Edit carefully for grammar, style, and formality appropriate to a government voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and Accessible Vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: Your press release should be accessible and easy to read for all constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vocabulary understandable across different education levels; avoid jargon or technical language that could alienate parts of the community. Prioritize plain language and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a Catchy Yet Informative Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a title that will attract readers and constituents to engage with your press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include your municipality name and a brief description of the announcement. Be creative but informative (example: “Rockland County, NY Deployed Report‑A‑Concern Module With GovPilot To Streamline Government Operations”). Ensure the title signals the news clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a Summary Subject Line
rubrics_metrics.description: The first sentence in your press release should come before, and separated from your body paragraphs. This sentence is meant to summarize the most vital information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer the question “What is this PR about?” in a single summary line so readers can retain the key point at a glance. Use a concise one‑sentence lead that captures the who/what/why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create Body Paragraphs With Clear/Straightforward Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Hook readers early with a catchy title and subject line, then fill your press release with vital and valuable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the reader's time—be direct and avoid writing a novel. Body should include all relevant information and be approximately 1–1½ pages long. Organize in clear, short paragraphs and prioritize the most important facts first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell Readers Where To Get More Information
rubrics_metrics.description: After your constituents have read your announcement, they may want to learn more about the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any sources referenced, with source information and URLs. Provide contact details or pointers to pages where readers can access deeper information to encourage engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plug Local Government Website
rubrics_metrics.description: Close your press release with a list of resources for constituents to navigate to for further updates and announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List local government social media accounts (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, etc.) and website links so residents know where to find ongoing information. Keep those social accounts and the website updated regularly so constituents can reference and share posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share Press Release on a Distribution Site
rubrics_metrics.description: Use distribution websites to distribute your articles, announcements, and press releases to a relevant audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms like EINPresswire and PR NewsWire act as intermediaries between the government and local publications; they help amplify reach to local and regional media outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Your Press Release on Social Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media is widely used daily and makes information easily shareable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share the press release across social platforms to maximize visibility and enable constituents to repost. Tailor copy and assets (images, links) for each platform to increase engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send Press Release To Relevant Parties (Email Campaigns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider email campaigns as part of your local government marketing strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mailing lists and targeted emails (e.g., sign‑up lists, business owner lists) to reach people with a specific interest. Direct emails help the most interested parties see the announcement immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Your Press Release on Your Local Government Website
rubrics_metrics.description: Your press release should live on your local government website so constituents can always find it in a stable location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an archive or news section on the municipal website; ensure posts are easy to find and linked from home page or news feed so regular visitors can discover updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define Subject Matter and Ensure Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing a press release, first define your subject matter and ensure you have the most accurate information to share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a simple workflow: define subject → write → edit → post on distribution channels → share. Verify facts before publishing to avoid misinformation and preserve trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate Topics for Local Government Press Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Local government press releases can cover a wide range of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical subjects include weather announcements, current events, community happenings, election dates, and new policies. Use press releases for newsworthy items relevant to constituents.
